reason: The text passage (Exodus 16) focuses on the people's failure to keep God's commandments regarding the Sabbath observance. When God addresses the issue of people gathering manna on the seventh day (which they were commanded not to do), the responsibility is placed directly on the people themselves: 'How long will you [plural - the people] refuse to keep My commandments and My teachings?' The passage presents Moses and the leadership as intermediaries receiving God's instructions to relay to the people, but does not attribute the people's disobedience to any failure of leadership. The blame is consistently directed at the people's own refusal to obey, not at their leaders' shortcomings.
